prerequisites: Física y Matemáticas I y II

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Knowledge and use of the principles of the strength of materials.

Acquire knowledge of the basic principles of elasticity and strength of materials: stress, tension and deformation; study of the behavior of deformable solids with different models; properties of the elastic solid: resistance and stiffness; experimental methods of stress and strain analysis in elastic solids.
Apply the acquired knowledge in the design, execution and maintenance of structural components.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Internal forces in continuous media. Concept of stress. Principal stresses. Statically determined stresses.
Topic 2. Deformations in solids. Physical concept of deformation. Longitudinal and angular deformation. Compatibility. Symmetries in deformations.
Topic 3. Mohr's circles. Mohr's circles in stresses. Mohr's circles in deformations.
Topic 4. Linear Elasticity. Fundamental hypotheses of the elastic solid. Constitutive equations. Hooke's Law. The elastic problem.
Topic 1. Efforts. Equilibrium conditions. Solicitations. Ligatures and characteristic reactions. Normal stresses.
Topic 2. Tension, compression and shear. Pure shear stresses.
Topic 3. Torsion. Torsional moments. Torsion of simple geometry sections.
Topic 4. Bending. Shear stress and bending moment diagrams. Pure bending: Navier's Law. Simple bending: Shear Formula. Deformations. Elastic equation.
Topic 6. Hyperstatic bending. Degree of hyperstaticity. Resolution methods.

assessment_methods.method: Short questions test proposed in class and submitted via virtual classroom
Delivery of exercises proposed in class and submitted via virtual classroom

assessment_rules: The overall passing mark for the course is a weighted average of 5/10. The short questions and exercise submissions (10% each) are non-reevaluable and have no minimum score. The laboratory practice test (20%) and the final exam (60%) require a minimum score of 5/10, are reevaluable, and failing the minimum on the final exam results in failing the course. Students can retake failed reevaluable activities in the extraordinary call; the advanced call consists of two written tests (50% each) with a minimum of 4 points.
